dedupe_keys.name: global wildland urban interface maps at 30 m for 2000 2010 and 2020 globeland30 based

description: These maps delineate the global wildland-urban interface at 30 m resolution for 2000, 2010 and 2020, defining it as places where 200 m buffers around artificial surfaces intersect 400 m buffers around forest, shrubland and grassland. Yongxuan Guo, Jianghao Wang, Yong Ge and Chenghu Zhou of the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, derived them from GlobeLand30 land cover and published them with a 2024 Science Advances paper, which finds the global interface grew by 35.6 percent since 2000 to 1.93 million km2 in 2020, mostly through urban expansion, with small fires in these areas rising since 2010. Coverage is global. Format and access: zipped raster tiles in the GlobeLand30 projection on Zenodo; the file list read shows archives for 2000 and 2020 and a sample. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: results inherit GlobeLand30 classification errors, earlier years have fewer inputs, and the buffer rule differs from housing-density definitions such as SILVIS. It supports wildfire exposure analysis of buildings, power lines and roads at the urban edge. Related catalogue records are the SILVIS wildland-urban interface maps for the US and Wildfire Risk to Communities.
